They were also using much of their living space as a warehouse for all of the donations for the Juarez families, she said. And "through the generosity of the community," enough donations of food, clothes and toys were collected to fill a 20-foot shipping container and a 16-foot cube truck -- including more than 75,000 cans of food, Dominici said. "That's the whole point here," Pennington said. "To give her what she needs to make her life easier to literally spread dreams and hope to people who have absolutely none of either one of those." "If you teach them and train them as a child and they go out and do the same, we would live in a much better world." Actress Selena Gomez introduced and presented Ruiz with her CNN Hero award. Each of the top 10 CNN Heroes also received $25,000.  Watch Ruiz accept her CNN Hero Award » . “When Ty Pennington came to our home and said, ‘Ruiz family, come on out,’ we all just ran out and couldn't believe that we were chosen,” Ruiz said. “It's a blessing to us, but we weren't expecting all of this at all, and it has been overwhelming.”

Pennington, the host of “Extreme Makeover: Home Edition,” said Ruiz and her family were chosen from among thousands of applicants across Texas. He explained that the goal was to provide Ruiz with what she most needed: the means to continue and expand her work.

Along with delivering supplies to residents of Juarez, Ruiz and her family have also been building a complex there that will include a community kitchen, an orphanage and a trade school.

Ruiz said her family had stopped work on their own home in 1996 so they could focus their energy on helping the Juarez community. As a result, many areas of their house remained incomplete. She also said much of their living space had been taken over by donated items meant for families in Juarez.

“A home is somewhere you can go after a long day's work and relax and where the family can get together and be able to sit down and talk about our day,” Ruiz said. “When we had the things in the living room, we couldn't do that there.”

When Ruiz and her family returned from the Bahamas, thousands of volunteers and local residents gathered around them. The show’s large bus kept the family from seeing the finished house until the crowd repeated the program’s famous line: “Move that bus!” Once the bus was moved, the Ruiz family saw their new home for the first time.

“For us, it is a new beginning, and it's going to change our lives,” Ruiz said.

“That's the whole point here,” Pennington said. “To give her what she needs to make her life easier to literally spread dreams and hope to people who have absolutely none of either one of those.”

For Ruiz, the mission is centered on guiding children so they can eventually help others in their own communities.

“If you teach them and train them as a child and they go out and do the same, we would live in a much better world,” she said.

Ruiz was first introduced to a worldwide audience when “CNN Heroes: An All-Star Tribute” premiered on Thanksgiving across CNN’s global networks. Actress Selena Gomez introduced Ruiz and presented her with her CNN Hero award. Each of the top 10 CNN Heroes received $25,000.

# Woman Who Delivers Supplies to Children in Juarez Receives Life-Changing Home Makeover

**By Staff Writer**

For years, Maria Ruiz has crossed the border with her car packed full of school supplies, food, clothing and hope.

A mother, volunteer and longtime advocate for children in Juarez, Mexico, Ruiz has spent much of her life making sure children in need have the basic items many families take for granted. Week after week, she has collected donations from neighbors, churches and local businesses, then delivered them to children living in some of the region’s most vulnerable communities.

But while Ruiz was busy helping others, her own home had fallen into disrepair.

That changed when Ty Pennington and the team from *Extreme Makeover: Home Edition* arrived with a surprise that left Ruiz and her family overwhelmed: a custom-built home designed to honor her service and give her family a safe, comfortable place to live.

The *Extreme Makeover* team transformed Ruiz’s aging house into a custom-built home suited to her family’s needs and her ongoing charitable work. ## A CNN Heroes–style feature: Maria Ruiz’s new foundation for hope

For years, Maria Ruiz built her life around other families’ needs.

In Juarez, where hardship can arrive quietly and stay for generations, Ruiz became the kind of person people turned to when they had nowhere else to go. She helped families facing poverty, instability and uncertainty — offering food, support, comfort and a reminder that they had not been forgotten.

Her work was not glamorous. It was often exhausting, emotional and done without much attention. But for the families she helped, Ruiz’s compassion could mean the difference between despair and a new beginning.

Then, unexpectedly, the spotlight found her.

After being honored for her service through CNN Heroes, Ruiz’s life changed in ways she never imagined. The recognition brought national attention to her mission — and to the personal sacrifices behind it. People who had never met her learned about the families she served in Juarez and the quiet determination that drove her to keep helping, even when her own resources were limited.

But the biggest surprise came when “Extreme Makeover: Home Edition” stepped in.

The show, known for transforming the homes of people who have given deeply to others, gave Ruiz and her family a new home — a place of safety, stability and dignity after years of focusing on everyone else’s needs.

For Ruiz, the gift was more than walls, windows and a roof. It was a turning point.

A new home meant her family could breathe. It meant a secure place to gather, rest and dream. It meant that after years of pouring herself into the lives of others, Ruiz was finally receiving the kind of care she had so often given away.

The makeover also amplified her mission. With more attention on her story, Ruiz’s work became a symbol of what can happen when ordinary people choose to respond to suffering with action. Her recognition helped show that heroism is not always dramatic. Sometimes it looks like a woman crossing boundaries of comfort and convenience to stand beside families in crisis.

Those who know Ruiz say the honors did not change her heart. They simply gave her more room to continue the work she already believed in.

Her story is a reminder that service can transform both the giver and the community — and that when compassion is recognized, it can ripple far beyond one family, one neighborhood or one city.

Maria Ruiz spent years helping families find hope.

Then, for once, hope came home to her.
